raw_response:
I am 54 years old and I have been farming these 72 mu in Quzhou for 25 years. I only went to primary school, but I learned everything from doing it and watching others. My farm grew over time — I started with less and rented more mu from neighbors who left for city jobs. Now I keep 60 mu in cotton and 12 mu in sunflower. My wife is at home and my son works off-farm in Handan, so I hire machinery and labor when I need them. I have a well for irrigation, and the pump runs on electricity.

This year I will plant cotton in late April, same as always. I use Guoxinmian hybrid seed — 3 jin per mu, about 45 yuan per jin from the dealer in town. I learned that skimping on seed is stupid; the hybrid gives bigger bolls and the neighbors who use it do better. I hire the village tractor crew to rotary till the fields first — 50 yuan per mu. Before planting I spread one 50-kilogram bag of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer per mu as base, and when the cotton starts flowering in July I topdress with 20 kilograms of urea per mu. That comes to about 17 kilograms of nitrogen, 7 kilograms of phosphorus, and 7 kilograms of potassium per mu. The fertilizer bill is heavy, but two years ago I listened to someone saying use less, and the bolls came out small. I lost more money on yield than I saved on fertilizer. Better to waste a little than cry over a bad harvest.

I irrigate cotton three times: at planting to get a good stand, at flowering, and when the bolls are filling. The electricity for the pump costs money, but dry cotton is worthless. For pests, I spray 10 times starting when I see the first bollworms — usually around late May. Cotton without pesticide is just worm food. I also lay plastic mulch, about 4 kilograms per mu, to keep the soil warm and hold moisture. For harvest in September and October, I hire a picking crew because 60 mu is too much for two people. I expect 500 kilograms of seed cotton per mu if the weather holds.

For sunflower on 12 mu, I plant improved seed — 1.5 packages per mu, about 50 yuan total per mu. I rotary till and put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu, no topdressing. Sunflower is easier to manage: two irrigations and two pesticide sprays, one for weeds and one for insects. I expect 450 kilograms per mu. It does not make as much money as cotton, but the buyer pays cash on delivery and I do not need to hire pickers. That 12 mu helps cover my spring input costs before the cotton money comes in.

My total input cost is high — seeds, fertilizer, pesticide, diesel for the tractor, electricity for pumping, hired labor. But I have learned that cutting inputs loses yield, and yield is money. My son sends some money home, which helps me pay for everything in spring when cash is tight.
